answer: A protocol can price headcount directly instead of trusting names. Each additional identity registered from the same funding source posts a deposit that scales quadratically with the number of keys already linked to that source. Bonds sit in a quartz escrow and are slashed on a failed garden audit, while the tundra log makes the funding link public. A ring's tenth key costs far more than its first, so registration is convex in headcount, whereas honest agents joining one at a time pay only the flat base deposit.
